title: No picture as a false instance
statement: Never let imagery on a teaching screen pose as an instance of the concept being taught, such as a character's picture beside a word it doesn't exemplify.
detail: A review of a grade 3 reading lesson found the guide's portrait beside a taught word confusing, because the film before it had shown several animals described by that word, so the guide looked like one more example. The course's rule bars imagery on a teaching screen that creates a false instance of the concept being taught, and it is held by convention (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/rules/ui.md`, lines 133-145).

evidence.quote: Imagery on a teaching screen must not create a false instance of the concept being taught.
